checks.guidance: Head-to-cotter-hole minus the sourced clamped column. What is left over must cover the pitch-link eye PLUS the nut's thread-start-to-castellation distance; both are unsourced, so this is a budget, not a verdict on the joint. It passes with 11.1435 mm worst case available. It cannot settle the joint: with a slotted nut and a cotter pin the constraint is slot-vs-hole ALIGNMENT, which quantises acceptable grip -- see the referenced stack's notes.

notes: The selection combines both stack paths this check needs (`head_to_cotter_hole` and `clamped_stack_sourced`) into ONE chain rather than composing two separately-summed StudyResults, because this topology puts every dimension on one connected graph -- there is no cross-study composition here for `docs/DAG_TOPOLOGY.md`'s fenced deliverable-4 concern to apply to.

The chain walks `cotter_hole_from_point` AGAINST its authored orientation (bolt_point -> cotter_hole_centerline, sign -1, i.e. it enters this study reversed), then `bolt_length_11` WITH its orientation (head_bearing_face -> bolt_point, sign -1 relative to this study's direction... entered from bolt_point going to head_bearing_face, i.e. against its own authored direction, sign -1 contributing +bolt_length_11 when read from this study's from-node), then the three clamped edges WITH their authored orientation (sign +1 each). Read end to end from `washer_far_face`: +washer, +pitch_plate_flange, +bushing_214820 is the wrong order to state signs in prose -- the authoritative signs are whatever `traverse()` derives from the graph, and `tests/test_topology_conversions.py` pins the resulting total against the stack's own published check rather than trusting this paragraph.
